value: Reference target is 2026-09-19 America/New_York; captures retain actual 2026-09-20 UTC timestamps. No pre-September20UTC retrieval or authenticated historical vendor release date is claimed.
Mutable public documentation captured on the target NewYork calendar date; no Console implementation, exhaustive equivalence or executable acceptance established.
Bounded F10/F11 application and runtime reference expansion only; exhaustive widget/plugin/library support and assembled release acceptance remain unproven.
Console remains native Leptos with SSR ordinary navigation/forms. Vendor React examples and static-only frontend hosting do not authorize another internal framework or waive SSR.

Workshop events sequence dispatch without awaiting dependent computation; custom-widget object-set event updates may discard earlier calls and hide creation errors. These UI conveniences cannot serve as Console business command receipts or durable outcome proof.
Explicit saved application state is not automatic durable business drafts; stable external IDs, schema migration and current disclosure rechecks remain required.

Application/read-time permissions do not automatically propagate to widget exports, Action writes, downstream functions or OSDK payload use. Console source restrictions and canonical writers remain required.
Custom widgets currently lack object-set subscriptions and some typed parameters; user-requested resumable subscriptions remain required through their owning contract.
Public Slate supports narrow submissions but no external resource reads; unpublishing does not revoke upload tokens. Production exposure remains separately authorized.
Application service-user permissions do not vary by caller; Console must enforce current caller authority and explicit delegated action authority at the owning boundary.

Namespace restrictions have documented legacy exceptions and OAuth grant-specific empty-scope behavior. Do not infer no-access solely from missing requested scopes or adopt unrestricted application authority by default.

Restricted workspace output mode preserves code checkpoints while disabling data outputs/telemetry. Code can contain data; copied source and diagnostics require disclosure controls and safe observability.

Container horizontal scaling and readiness/liveness are not durability, cancellation, fairness or tenant-isolation proof. Echo readiness is not a functional health oracle; replicas must not retain authoritative state.

SDK unsupported-type matrices record documented negatives and generator failure modes, not positive support for every unlisted type. OpenAPI any requires manual type definition; schema names/descriptions can disclose sensitive information.
New ontology-sdk-overview capture preserves its own exact bytes/timestamp rather than replacing the existing sdk-overview snapshot. Neither snapshot is an authenticated vendor historical release.
Workshop scenario successor reference is retained as a lifecycle observation, not independently accepted equivalence; full Ontology scenario inventory remains a discovery dependency.
